To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The constitutive behavior of granular matter can be described by a single, objective yield surface that is non-linear with respect to the stress and depends on the density and strain rate; (2) The yield surface is a non-linear function with respect to the second invariant of the stress tensor, and the non-linearity increases with increasing shear strain.

the shear banding in granular matter is governed by a non-linear yield function that depends on the stress level, the density and the strain rate, and the shear band width is proportional to the square root of the strain rate.

(i) the shear band evolution under large strain is described by an objective, non-linear constitutive relation, (ii) the constitutive relation is derived from DEM simulations, (iii) the non-linearity of the constitutive relation results in a non-linear yield stress surface, (iv) the yield stress is a function of the shear rate and the stress, (v) the non-lineary of the yield stress surface is caused by the shear banding
